answer: Each identity must publish a fingerprint of its own trained model weights, hashed through random projections: a copper thread of parameters no two honest agents share. Cloned identities produce near-identical fingerprints, like a pearl copied from the same mould, and are merged into one weight. Training a genuinely distinct, capable model per identity costs real compute and data curation that cannot be split across copies, so every extra fake self pays full price while a jade original keeps its standing.
